correctness.rationale: Invariant-common-domain decomposition proved in both directions; C_2×C_2 orbits enumerate all indecomposable blocks; prescribed-product count follows from involutions in S_f ×(C_2 wr S_t) plus a disjoint complement. Marked EGF checked exhaustively for all n≤6 and every actual product fiber. For the CLT, all nonzero quartic saddle directions are suppressed by positive lower terms; perturbation of the positive saddle and its prefactor is controlled uniformly, and the moment-generating function converges to exp(s²/2).

originality.rationale: The natural object and general commutation question are established in arXiv:1205.1664v1; the examined primary texts do not supply the prescribed-product fiber count and Gaussian defect limit for uniformly random commuting self-inverse partial bijections. Lugo 2009 concerns unrestricted involution composition in a group, and Kiefer–Leemans concerns total group involutions up to conjugacy. The exact statement is not a formal restatement or direct corollary of those results; an unlocated specialized enumeration remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An unlocated table of commuting partial involutions or a direct conditional-Gaussian theorem could cover part or all of the statement.
Generic analytic combinatorics could derive the CLT once the species inventory is supplied; the claim is the particular model and its explicit proof, not the abstract saddle method.
The external search inventory is finite, so absolute literature novelty cannot be guaranteed.

value.rationale: The rank of the product of commuting partial bijections is intrinsic to a classical inverse monoid. Determining its typical defect and nontrivial n^{1/4} Gaussian fluctuations for the uniform conditional distribution addresses an asymptotic gap not answered by commuting-graph results. Complete cycle-refined counts and individual product fibers are natural finer structural invariants, not arbitrary parameter slices.
